title: Electrical Position Sensing and Dual Confirmation for the Engine Fire Handle
abstract: Replaces the single microswitch behind the fire handle with a dual sensing arrangement and reports the handle position to the crew, so that a partially latched handle is annunciated rather than discovered on a walk round.

sections.reason: The detent introduced by the current standard removed the stable intermediate position, but the handle position is still sensed by a single microswitch and there is no indication of handle state other than the fire warning itself. During the service introduction of the detent, two handles were found with a microswitch out of adjustment after the modification, which would not have been detected until the handle was next pulled. A control this critical should not depend on a single switch and a maintenance adjustment, and the certification office has asked whether the position can be sensed independently.
sections.description: The single microswitch behind each fire handle is replaced by two independent proximity sensors reading the same target, wired to separate inputs, and the handle position is annunciated on the overhead panel when the two disagree or when the handle is out of the stowed position without a fire warning. The link D7620110697976 is retained and the tube assembly D7620118982319 is modified to carry the sensor target. The fitting KAD86061-43 introduced with the guard is renewed with a sensor mounting boss. Wiring at FIN 57EC and FIN 90EC is replaced by a four-wire run and a new feed is added at FIN 2EC5. Work is on the overhead panel in zones 481, 432 and 411, with detail on drawings D76201138009 and D76200031513. The extinguishing discharge path is unchanged.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 1.3 kg per aircraft for all four handles. Electrical load rises by 25 volt-amperes for the sensor supply. The dual sensing arrangement requires the detent standard as a prerequisite because the sensor target is carried on the modified tube assembly. Dispatch changes: a single sensor failure becomes a new minimum equipment list item that does not exist today, and that entry has to be written and agreed. Crew documentation, maintenance, troubleshooting and wiring content all require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Launched and in detailed design. Production cut-in is planned for the next available slot with retrofit offered afterwards. Retrofit is expected to be one shift for all four handles with the overhead panel dropped, on aircraft already at the detent standard.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether a new minimum equipment list entry can be agreed for a single sensor failure or whether the aircraft must be treated as no-dispatch, whether the annunciation can be added to the overhead panel without a new lamp, and whether the sensor target can be carried on the current tube assembly without re-opening the detent substantiation.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in planned at next available slot
